title: Getting Started
html:
This offline seed is a concise project-authored summary for retrieval smoke tests. Stardew Valley is open-ended, so early priorities should balance a small crop plot, daily energy, exploration, and income rather than trying to complete every activity immediately.

Preparing the first harvest

On most farm maps, the player begins with Parsnip Seeds. Clear a small area, till the soil, plant the seeds, and water them every day. Crops that are not watered do not grow that day. Parsnips take four growing days, so calendar planning matters near the end of a season.

First spring priorities

Build a chest early, meet villagers, forage while travelling, and use spare energy for fishing or clearing the farm. Avoid planting more crops than can be watered reliably. The Mines become an important source of ore after they open, while the Community Center introduces longer-term collection goals.

Energy and planning

Tools consume energy, and a day has limited time. Keep enough energy and travel time to return safely. Upgrade tools and expand the farm gradually instead of maximizing crop count on the first days.

title: Bundles
html:
This offline seed summarizes the purpose of Community Center bundles. Bundles are item donations requested by the Junimos. Completing a bundle gives an individual reward, while completing every bundle in a room unlocks a larger world or community upgrade.

Standard and remixed bundles

Standard and Remixed Bundles are different game setups and must not be mixed. The selected bundle mode is chosen when the save is created. A reliable answer should use the bundle mode stored in the player's state or ask for clarification when it matters.

Route choice

Purchasing a JojaMart Membership replaces the Community Center restoration path with Joja development projects. Recommendations about bundle completion therefore depend on whether the save follows the Community Center route or the Joja route.

Planning collections

Bundle requirements may depend on season, weather, item quality, access to later areas, or optional choices within a bundle. Store required items before their season ends and verify exact requirements against the structured bundle facts.

title: The Mines
html:
This offline seed summarizes the normal Mines. The entrance becomes available early in the first spring after the landslide is cleared. The Mines contain 120 floors, and deeper floors provide different enemies, materials, and increasing access to ore.

Preparing for a mine trip

Bring food for energy and health, leave unnecessary inventory at home, and allow enough time to return before the end of the day. A pickaxe is required for rocks, while a weapon is needed for monsters.

Progression goals

Mine trips should balance reaching deeper floors with collecting ore and surviving. Ore upgrades tools and crafting equipment, but pushing too far without food or weapon upgrades can waste the day. Treat mining as one part of the broader farm progression.

Failure and recovery

Running out of health can cause lost items and gold. The Adventurer's Guild provides an item-recovery service for one lost item or stack after a mine defeat, so valuable losses are not always permanent.

title: Fishing
html:
This offline seed summarizes the fishing skill and mini-game. After a bite, keep the fish icon inside the green catch bar until the progress meter fills. Short taps and controlled movement are often easier than holding the button continuously.

Improving consistency

Fishing skill increases the size of the catch bar and improves the activity over time. Better rods, bait, tackle, food buffs, and practice can make difficult fish more manageable.

Availability conditions

Individual fish may require a specific season, weather, time window, location, or special condition. These conditions should be answered from structured fish records rather than inferred from this general guide.

Early-game use

Fishing can provide income and experience when crops are already watered or when the player has spare time and energy. It is one option among farming, foraging, mining, quests, and social activities.
